one_liner: Cloud team chat (channels, DMs, files, calls) with a free workspace, an HTTP API via API keys and OAuth2 app tokens, and a vendor-hosted MCP server at mcp.pumble.com.

auth.notes: The integration path the SDK documents for an app acting for workspace users is OAuth2 (consent screen, then an access token and bot token). access.notes: Cloud only. Anyone can open a free workspace (owner of that workspace). The API addon and custom-app credentials are documented as available on all plans, and a free workspace may install up to 3 addons. Only owners and admins can install apps, so a member in someone else’s workspace may be blocked unless an admin installs the addon or turns off the optional “request app approval” setting. Marketplace listing review was not verified.

api.notes: There is a documented HTTP API, not SDK-only. The API-key addon covers sending and replying to messages, reactions, deletion, channel creation, and listing channels and messages. one_liner: Discord offers self-serve app registration, a broad cloud API with OAuth2 and bot-token authentication, community MCP servers, and a Composio toolkit. Free credential eligibility is unverified, and some scopes and large-scale privileged intents require Discord approval.

auth.notes: OAuth2 is used to act on behalf of a user. Its bearer token is not a separate authentication method. Bot tokens authenticate as the bot itself and are used for most REST calls and Gateway connections. HTTP Basic with the client ID and secret applies only to OAuth2 token endpoints.

access.notes: Discord documents self-serve app registration and bot-token generation, but the cited onboarding flow does not explicitly confirm that a free account can obtain working credentials. api.notes: The public REST API supports read and write operations on core resources including channels, guilds, users, and messages. The separate bidirectional Gateway WebSocket carries real-time events.

one_liner: Telegram supports bot-scoped messaging, but a bot token does not grant access to a user’s personal inbox or full chat history.

auth.notes: An MTProto user-authorized session lets an integration call the Telegram API as the user. The app’s api_id and api_hash are required for authorization but do not sign the user in. A BotFather token authenticates the bot, not the user. A separately authorized business connection lets a bot handle updates and send messages on the user’s behalf within its permissions. Telegram Gateway accepts a bearer token for verification-code delivery. Telegram Login uses OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with OpenID Connect for sign-in; its optional telegram:bot_access scope lets the linked bot send direct messages to the user, not read their chats.

access.notes: Register a free bot through @BotFather to obtain a token for the hosted Bot API. Standard messaging is free within rate limits, with optional paid broadcasts for higher volume. MTProto requires an active Telegram account and app registration at my.telegram.org. Running the Bot API server locally replaces the API endpoint, not Telegram’s hosted messaging service.

api.notes: The Bot API uses method-oriented HTTPS/JSON endpoints to send and edit messages, forward media, look up chats, and receive updates by webhook or polling. Bots ordinarily cannot start private conversations, see only relevant group messages by default, and cannot retrieve full chat history from the update queue. MTProto provides broader user-client access, including message history and contacts.

mcp.notes: No Telegram-published MCP server was found. The community package @iqai/mcp-telegram uses a BotFather token and supports sending, forwarding, pinning, and chat lookup. Composio advertises a separate managed MCP option.

verdict.rationale: Free, self-serve credentials and a documented API make bot-scoped messaging practical, but a bot token does not grant access to a user’s personal inbox or full chat history. Before using Telegram conversations in an agent, review Telegram’s content-licensing terms, which restrict AI use of platform data and describe possible exceptions based on ongoing, context-specific consent from all relevant users.

one_liner: Meta's hosted WhatsApp Business Platform (Cloud API) is a broad Graph REST API that a developer can start calling with self-serve tokens and a free test number, with an official beta MCP server as well as a Composio toolkit.

auth.notes: The Cloud API is called with a bearer access token. For a direct developer acting on their own business, Meta recommends a long-lived System User access token; user access tokens (from the App Dashboard, Graph API Explorer, or Facebook Login) are supported but short-lived, and Tech Providers/partners use Business Integration System User tokens obtained by exchanging an Embedded Signup code from Facebook Login for Business.

access.notes: A developer registers, creates a Meta app, and gets a test WhatsApp account, test Messaging account, and test phone number that can send template messages with no payment method on file. Real usage is metered per delivered business-to-user message and needs a payment method and business verification; distributing an app to other businesses (Tech Provider) needs App Review. Cloud-hosted only.

api.notes: Cloud API (graph.facebook.com) sends and receives messages, calls, and groups; the Business Management API covers accounts, phone numbers, templates, billing, and analytics; webhooks deliver inbound events. The reference is readable without login.

mcp.notes: Meta hosts "WhatsApp Business Tools" at https://mcp.facebook.com/whatsapp_business_tools, authenticated by Meta developer OAuth, labelled beta, and rolling out gradually. Community servers also exist (for example the LobeHub whatsapp-mcp-server and GreenAPI-based servers), but the vendor server is usable now.

verdict.rationale: A developer can register, create an app, and call the Cloud API with a generated token against an auto-provisioned test number that needs no payment method, and the public API covers messaging, templates, accounts, media, and webhooks. Production sending is per-message billed and requires a payment method, and the official MCP server is beta and not yet available to every account.

one_liner: Aircall is a cloud-only business phone system with a broad public REST API (Basic Auth for your own account, OAuth for multi-customer apps), but working credentials require a paid customer account; its own MCP server is an official beta that an account manager must enroll you in.

auth.notes: The docs explicitly offer two methods and recommend Basic Authentication when you are connecting your own internal tools or private integration, which is the path a third-party agent acting for one user takes. OAuth is reserved for apps distributed to many customers and requires joining the Technology Partner Program. The resulting access token is sent as a Bearer token, but that is the OAuth grant, not a separately documented token method.

access.notes: API keys are generated from the dashboard of an existing Aircall account (Integrations → API keys), and the pricing FAQ says all plans include API access. auth.notes: Integrations acting on behalf of users use the OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow. Short-lived user tokens last one hour and can be exchanged for refreshable 60-day tokens. The client-credentials flow supports app-level operations such as oEmbed and does not replace user consent.

one_liner: WooCommerce is an open-source ecommerce platform for WordPress with a production-ready REST API and an official MCP integration in developer preview.

auth.notes: For merchant integrations over HTTPS, use HTTP Basic Auth with the Consumer Key as the username and the Consumer Secret as the password. access.notes: On a free self-hosted installation, enable non-Plain permalinks and generate keys under WooCommerce → Settings → Advanced → REST API. A separate community plugin offers a public, read-only storefront server without access to private orders or customers.

one_liner: BigCommerce is a cloud ecommerce platform with a broad public API. Its official shopper-facing MCP is generally available, while its merchant administration MCP is in early access.

auth.notes: Third-party apps use a modified OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow that issues a token per store. For a direct single-store integration, a merchant can provision a static access token and send it in the X-Auth-Token header; it functions like an API key, although BigCommerce classifies it as OAuth-based. GraphQL Storefront supports bearer tokens, and REST Storefront supports same-origin shopper-session authentication. HTTP Basic is documented for legacy accounts unavailable to new stores and for provider-hosted tax endpoints, not as a current authentication path into BigCommerce’s public store APIs.

access.notes: New developers can create scoped API credentials in a 15-day trial store. The current signup FAQ says a credit card is required, but there is no charge unless the user chooses to upgrade. one_liner: Devin is Cognition’s AI software engineer: it can write, run, and test code and can be controlled through a REST API or an official MCP server.

auth.notes: Devin recommends service-user API keys for production and shared integrations. Personal access tokens act as the users who created them and inherit their permissions. Both credential types are sent in the Authorization: Bearer header. The public API docs reviewed did not document an OAuth2 flow.

access.notes: Teams and standard non-enterprise organizations can provision a service user in Settings → Devin API. Teams is a self-serve paid plan, but the memo did not establish whether Free, a trial, or a lower-priced individual plan provides working API credentials. Free public-repository access through DeepWiki MCP does not grant access to the Devin platform API.

api.notes: The public v3 reference covers read and write operations for sessions, knowledge notes, secrets, schedules, and automations. Enterprise scope adds cross-organization administration, analytics, and audit logs. Use v3 for new integrations and avoid the deprecated playbook endpoints.

mcp.notes: Cognition hosts the Devin MCP server over Streamable HTTP. It exposes session controls, repository documentation and Q&A, knowledge, and schedules. It uses a cog_ bearer credential. Personal access tokens and enterprise service-user keys require X-Org-Id; organization-scoped service-user keys resolve the organization automatically. The legacy /sse transport is deprecated, not /mcp. DeepWiki MCP is a separate, free, unauthenticated service for public-repository documentation.

verdict.rationale: Devin has a broad, publicly documented REST API, an official hosted MCP server, and a documented credential path for Teams and standard organizations. The most accessible plan that grants working API credentials remains unverified.

one_liner: Higgsfield offers a hosted image-and-video generation API, an official MCP connector, and a Composio toolkit.

auth.notes: The REST API uses a key ID and secret. The separate MCP product uses OAuth authorization.

access.notes: This is the closest category for self-service, prepaid access to working generation. Higgsfield says no plan or subscription is required, but developers must fund a balance with a $5 minimum top-up.

api.notes: The reference covers model-specific generation schemas, request status, and cancellation.

mcp.notes: The connector uses OAuth and the signed-in Higgsfield account, separately from API-key billing.

verdict.rationale: Developers can sign up for an API account and use documented generation endpoints. Requests are paid from a prepaid balance, although Higgsfield says no plan or subscription is involved.

evidence.quote: Create and manage API credentials in Higgsfield Console . Each credential consists of a key ID and a secret.
MCP connects through OAuth authorization, no API key is needed. API keys belong to the Higgsfield API, a separate developer product.
Sign up for an API account, either as an individual or as a company. Register a payment method and fund your balance.
Billing is pay-as-you-go from a US dollar balance, and the minimum top-up is $5.
No plan or subscription is involved: fund the balance, send requests at the rates listed in the catalog, and new requests simply wait once the balance hits zero.
The API reference is generated from the public OpenAPI specification. It includes model-specific generation schemas plus the shared status and cancellation operations.
This guide uses the REST API so you can see the complete request lifecycle. It takes about five minutes.
Higgsfield connects to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and other MCP-compatible agents, with no API key. In Claude, add a custom connector with the URL https://mcp.higgsfield.ai/mcp .
Higgsfield AI provides asynchronous image and video generation APIs powered by multiple creative AI models.
The Higgsfield API lets you generate video and images from your own code: one API key opens every model in the API catalog, and each request is paid in US dollars from a prepaid balance.

problems: The access categories have no exact value for self-service credentials with prepaid usage but no subscription.

The API FAQ describes account creation and credential generation without mentioning payment, while the getting-started article instructs developers to fund the balance before generating a key. The funded route is used because the classification concerns working generation requests.
name: higgsfield

verification.note: The API docs show credentials as a key ID plus secret, so api_key as the only and primary API method is fair. The OAuth quote is explicitly for the separate MCP product, not another recommended API method.

Quotes show self-serve signup but require a payment method and a prepaid balance with a $5 minimum top-up, and they deny any free path. That is not a subscription, which the quotes state outright, but paid_plan is the only defined level for must-pay access with no free or trial path.
A public OpenAPI reference and a quickstart that uses the REST API prove rest and public docs. Generation schemas plus status and cancellation do not contradict moderate breadth.
Higgsfield's own help page tells users to add the connector at https://mcp.higgsfield.ai/mcp now, so official and generally_available are shown. Nothing quoted calls it beta, pilot, or unlaunched.
The cited Composio docs page describes a Higgsfield toolkit for image and video generation APIs.

Documented REST access exists and signup is self-serve, but working requests require funding a prepaid balance, so buildable_with_caveats with main_blocker paid_plan follows from the judged auth, access, and api values.

one_liner: Mermaid CLI is an installable diagram-rendering tool with a local Node.js API, not an API-backed account service.

auth.notes: The documented interfaces use local files, stdin, or Node.js. The README does not explicitly state that authentication is unnecessary.

access.notes: The license permits anyone to use the software free of charge, and the README describes a local CLI that takes a diagram file as input and generates an output file. This local use does not require API credentials.

api.notes: The public README documents local diagram rendering through Node.js, not an HTTP API for account objects.

mcp.notes: A third-party wrapper invokes Mermaid CLI. Mermaid Chart’s hosted MCP server serves a separate service.

verdict.rationale: Credentials are self-serve, but the API is narrow.

evidence.quote: It's possible to call mermaid-cli via a Node.JS API. Please be aware that the NodeJS API is not covered by semver , as mermaid-cli follows mermaid 's versioning.

one_liner: TranscriptAPI.com is a hosted service that retrieves existing YouTube captions as timestamped text or JSON and helps agents discover videos through search, channels, and playlists.

auth.notes: The REST API uses a vendor-issued API key sent as a Bearer credential. OAuth 2.1 is documented for MCP, not for REST.

access.notes: New accounts receive 100 free credits without a payment card and can obtain an API key from the dashboard. The similarly named open-source Python package is separate from the hosted service.

api.notes: The read-only API supports transcript retrieval, YouTube search, channel browsing, and playlist extraction. Transcript retrieval requires an existing caption track; the API does not transcribe raw audio.

mcp.notes: The vendor-hosted server offers 12 tools, supports OAuth 2.1 or API-key authentication, and shares the REST API account and credits.

verdict.rationale: Developers can use free self-serve credits or the vendor’s hosted MCP server to discover YouTube videos and retrieve existing captions. The read-only API cannot generate missing transcripts or manage YouTube content.

evidence.quote: The API uses Bearer token authentication. Include your API key in the Authorization header of every request:
100 free credits to try the API — no card required.
You can start for free: new accounts get 100 free credits, no card required, and one transcript costs one credit.
Get YouTube video transcripts through our REST API or seamlessly integrate with AI assistants using Model Context Protocol (MCP).
TranscriptAPI is a hosted REST API, separate from the open-source YouTubeTranscriptApi Python package, which fetches transcripts from your own machine.

The YouTube Transcript API provides a simple and reliable way to extract transcripts from YouTube videos programmatically. This complete reference covers authentication, request parameters, response formats, and practical examples.
TranscriptAPI is managed and also adds YouTube search, channel browsing and playlist extraction.

TranscriptAPI runs a hosted (remote) MCP server at https://transcriptapi.com/mcp . Add that URL to an MCP client and your AI assistant can fetch YouTube transcripts, search YouTube, and list a channel’s or playlist’s videos.

Read one transcript job's current processing, completed, failed, or requires-ASR-confirmation state without creating work or waiting.
List, fetch, translate, and delete your stored transcripts, and list async jobs. All endpoints accept the same API-key auth.

one_liner: Grain is a hosted meeting-recording and notes service with a public API, an official MCP server, and a Composio toolkit.

auth.notes: OAuth2 is documented for integrations used by Grain users. Personal and workspace access tokens can also be sent as bearer tokens.

access.notes: Personal access tokens are available on the Free plan. Workspace-wide tokens require admin access and a Business or Enterprise plan.

api.notes: The publicly readable HTTP reference covers meeting data, recordings, highlights, uploads, and sharing.

mcp.notes: Grain documents an operating server and connection instructions; some capabilities depend on plan.

verdict.rationale: Personal API access is available on the Free plan, and the documented API can read meeting data and manage recordings. Workspace API access requires a Business or Enterprise plan and admin access.

evidence.quote: All data is hosted on AWS infrastructure in the USA within a dedicated virtual private cloud (VPC).

This authentication method is for developers building integrations with Grain to be used by any Grain users. The API supports a standard OAuth2 Authorization Code flow, including the PKCE extension for client-side only authentication.
To authenticate API calls, the client must add the following header:
Authorization: Bearer TOKEN

Personal Access Token (PAT) : grants access on behalf of a single user. The token has the same permissions as the user who generated it. Best for personal automations or testing. Available on every plan, including Free.
Requires admin access to generate and is available on Business and Enterprise plans.

The Grain API lets developers read meeting data, manage recordings, and receive real-time events from Grain programmatically. Use it to build custom integrations, sync data to internal systems, or automate workflows that go beyond what Grain's built-in integrations support.
The Grain API lets you read and manage recordings, highlights, uploads, and more.

Grain's MCP (Model Context Protocol) server gives AI assistants direct access to your meetings, transcripts, AI notes, and workspace data. Ask questions, generate reports, create clips, and organize recordings, all from your AI chat interface.
If everything is set up properly, you'll see Claude make requests to the available Grain tools that are needed to fulfill the data needs of the Chat request.
Grain records, transcribes, and organizes meetings so teams can review conversations, share insights, and manage meeting content.
Not for personal API access, which is available on every plan, including Free. Workspace API access is available on Business and Enterprise plans and requires admin access to generate.

Self-serve free personal credentials plus a documented API that reads meeting data and manages recordings meet buildable_now with no main blocker. Workspace access needing Business/Enterprise and admin is a narrower path, not the blocker.
